issues.text: The report notes the paper's framing and empirical approach to the mechanism analysis have problems, but the central structure is hard to follow: the manuscript alternates between many empirical approaches and units of analysis (OLS, IV, TWFE, heterogeneity), decreasing readability and making the argument harder to follow.
issues.quote: The paper combines a multitude of empirical approaches and units of analysis. Although each approach has its advantage, switching back and forth between different approaches decreases the manuscript's readability.

issues.text: The ordering of sections is suboptimal: biases are discussed in separate places (measurement biases in Section 2.3 while omitted variable and reverse causality biases appear only in Section 4.1), so biases should be addressed together after the empirical strategy.
issues.quote: Section 2.3 (Title should be: "Potential sources of *measurement* bias") deals with the potential measurement biases, while only section 4.1 addresses the omitted variable bias and reverse causality bias.

issues.text: The comparison between all taxa and non-bird taxa is incomplete because the bird-only group is missing; results for birds may be insignificant or point in a different direction, so all three samples (all, bird, non-bird) should be reported.
issues.quote: After the main results, you choose to contrast two samples: All taxa vs non-bird taxa. The comparison group is missing.

issues.text: The sectoral GDP results (Table 2) are considered highly biased and uninformative because disaggregating GDP and jointly including sectors increases problems of attribution, multicollinearity, reverse causality and omitted variable bias; the evaluator suggests dropping this analysis or using a different strategy.
issues.quote: Results on sectoral GDP (Table 2) are highly biased and, therefore not very informative.

issues.text: The selection of contributing counties in the pollution channel analysis is insufficiently justified: counties within 300 km are excluded even though nearby sources would seem most important, and the LASSO selects counties thousands of miles away, which may be a statistical artifact rather than a physical impact.
issues.quote: First, why are counties in a 300 km radius excluded? It would seem that close pollution sources are the most important.

issues.text: Figure 5 and its description are misleading, since LASSO-selected distant counties suggest possibly spurious relations, and the paper lacks natural science support for long-distance pollution transport.
issues.quote: Nonetheless, Figure 5 and your description is misleading at first sight.

issues.text: The land-use/protected area analysis would be stronger using a panel of protected area creation with a TWFE estimator, rather than the current approach.
issues.quote: The analysis of land-use policies (section 5.2) could be improved by using a panel of protected areas.

issues.text: The graphical presentation of main results (Figures 3a, 3b, 4b) makes it hard to see the sample structure, first-stage strength, and differences between IV and OLS estimates; results should be shown in tables with fixed effects and observation counts.
issues.quote: OLS and IV estimates are easier to compare in Table format - Figure 4b does not easily convey how good the IV strategy is (first stage)

issues.text: The pollution regulation analysis (section 5.1) includes extra GDP exercises and repeated comparisons of overall versus mechanism effects that seem to massage the data; it could be cut to the TWFE estimation only.
issues.quote: The exercises with GDP and the repeated comparison of overall vs. mechanism effects seems to massage the data a bit too much.

issues.text: The paper does not justify clearly why state-level analysis is the preferred spatial unit, and shifting units of analysis adds unnecessary complexity; one unit should be chosen for the main text.
issues.quote: Please provide a more straightforward argument why a state-level analysis is the preferred spatial unit.

issues.text: The interpretation of year fixed effects as capturing only common shocks such as national recessions is incomplete, since they also absorb common changes in federal environmental policy, regulation, protected-area financing and enforcement budgets.
issues.quote: Year fixed effecs also capture common changes in federal environmental policies, regulations, laws, financing of protected areas, overall enforcement budget, etc.

issues.text: Table A.2 is described as a panel regression although its outcome is constant over time in columns 2-6, which is unclear.
issues.quote: How is Table A.2 a panel regression if its outcome is constant over time (columns 2-6)?

issues.text: Table 2 does not specify which fixed effects are used.
issues.quote: Table 2 does not describe which FE are used.

issues.text: Figure A6 left shows a coefficient with the wrong sign, and Figure 3d is missing a zero reference line.
issues.quote: Figure A6 left has a wrong negative sign on the coefficient.

issues.text: The text mixes data description with estimation strategy (e.g., on page 9), which makes the paper harder to read.
issues.quote: Sometimes the paper mixes the data description with the estimation strategy
